name: CPLP Mobility Residence Permit (AR CPLP)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being a national of a CPLP (Community of Portuguese Language Countries) member state other than Portugal itself.
This now requires obtaining a consular visa in the country of origin before travel, plus security screening — the earlier in-country channel for CPLP nationals has effectively closed.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the consular visa from your country of origin.

outcome.duration_length: physical card valid 2 years, renewable for successive 3-year periods

sources.title: gov.pt — Acordo sobre a Mobilidade CPLP (Luanda, 17 Jul 2021), transposed by Lei n.º 18/2022
Diário da República — Lei n.º 9/2025 (13 Feb 2025), CPLP mobility reform

notes: CATEGORY JUDGMENT CALL, flagged honestly same as Germany's BNO route: this is nationality-based community mobility between Portuguese-speaking countries rooted in shared colonial-era history and language, not literal bloodline descent — 'ancestry' is the closest fit among the current 9 categories but arguably deserves its own bucket in a future schema pass, exactly the same open question flagged on uk_bno. GENUINE STRUCTURAL UPGRADE confirmed for 2026: the AR CPLP now grants Schengen free movement to its holders (previously CPLP-permit holders could NOT move freely within Schengen) — a real and significant rights expansion. GENUINE STRUCTURAL TIGHTENING also confirmed simultaneously: what was once a genuinely simplified/preferential in-country regularisation channel (manifestação de interesse style) now requires a prior consular visa obtained from the country of origin plus security screening — the 'previously not requiring...' framing many secondary sources still use is stale. gov.pt's own materials still advertise a '72-hour online issuance' for some cases, but the practical 2026 route is consular-visa-first — flagged as a live discrepancy between official marketing copy and the operative process, an unusual case of a government's OWN site containing outdated framing rather than a third-party site being stale.
